signal-green.purpose: #1E8A5B means 'reporting now' and is never decorative. #2FBF83 is the same state on charcoal. #166B47 (Signal Green Deep) is the ON-TINT TEXT derivation only — Signal Green on its own 12% tint measures 3.73:1, under the 4.5:1 floor for 10px status chips; the deep value measures 5.60:1. Never use it as a fill.

chatFidelity.note: Reproduces WhatsApp and iOS inside the AskDemo handset only. See DESIGN.md, 'Third-party UI fidelity'. Never use these outside the phone screen.

consoleLive.note: Live-telemetry accents inside the TraceModal/XenAuthModal night consoles only: live-signal green, its tints, Trace Blue tint, and the console's blue-black grounds. Never used on the page surfaces.

brandMarks.note: Official vendor logo colours, reproduced verbatim on the neutral bone plate per DESIGN.md 'Third-party brand marks'. Quoted artifacts, not tokens — never normalise toward the palette, never use outside a vendor's own mark.

display.purpose: Hero h1 only: Archivo 800 clamp(34px,4.2vw,58px) uppercase at wdth 125, line-height 1.02. The footer wordmark is the same voice as an SVG.

headline.purpose: Every section h2: Archivo 750 clamp(34px,4.4vw,56px) at wdth 110, line-height calc(1em+4px). A ratio line-height cannot be correct at both ends of a fluid clamp; a constant increment can.

title.purpose: Card and console h3: Archivo 700 clamp(24px,2.4vw,32px) at wdth 100, calc(1em+4px). Previously h3 inherited body 1.55 and computed 32px/49.6px.

price-anchor.purpose: The $10 lockup: 800, clamp(72px,7.5vw,108px), 0.86 line-height, tabular-nums. Compact clamp(44px,5.5vw,64px) in the comparison cost lockup.

body.purpose: All human-written copy: IBM Plex Sans 450 16px/1.6. Plex replaced Source Sans 3 because its 486 x-height against Archivo's 526 made body copy read pale, which is why 93 of 127 weight declarations had drifted to 700/800.

caption.purpose: Plex 450 13.5px/1.5 and Plex 500 12px/1.4. Two steps, not the six near-duplicates (15/14.5/14/13.5/13/12.5) that used to be smeared across the page.

machine.purpose: JetBrains Mono 500, ONLY where values must align in a column: serials, temperatures, timestamps, the API panel, and the loss register's citation column. 12px standard, 11px for citations (never smaller), 10px for axis graduations.

price-unit.purpose: The uppercase unit beside the $10 anchor: clamp(20px,1.8vw,26px) Archivo 700.

panel-title.purpose: h3 inside dark console panels (API band): clamp(22px,2.4vw,30px).

panel-headline.purpose: Heading inside a panel column (Platform console): clamp(28px,3.2vw,40px), never the section scale.

stage-title.purpose: h3 over the industries photo stage: clamp(22px,2.6vw,32px).

hero-lead.purpose: The 500-weight paragraph under the hero headline over footage: clamp(15px,1.2vw,16.5px)/1.55 at rgba(255,255,255,0.85), max 44ch — heavier than daylight body copy so it holds against moving video.

manifest-row.purpose: 13px cargo/location cells in the demo-fleet manifest.

manifest-serial.purpose: 12px mono serial with its leading state dot.

card-label.purpose: 11px mono uppercase label on the walkthrough's single annotation card.

card-value.purpose: 20px mono value on the walkthrough's annotation card.

step-caption.purpose: 19px Archivo title of a walkthrough caption-tab.

price-lockup.purpose: The comparison section's $10-vs-$30+ cost lockup: the page's largest non-hero numerals.
price-lockup.fontFamily: Archivo, Source Sans 3, Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, sans-serif

figure.purpose: Archivo 800 CONDENSED, three tiers, all tabular. figure clamp(52px,6vw,88px) wdth 82 — the single largest figure on a surface (the stakes band's $273,990 terminal). figure-headline clamp(38px,4.6vw,62px) wdth 80 — the stakes band's three-up magnitudes. figure-major clamp(28px,3vw,38px) wdth 86 — the comparison verdict and the connectivity numbers. Condensed 800 beside the page's extended 800 headings is its primary type contrast.

value.purpose: Archivo 700 17px wdth 92 tabular. In the comparison the XenTag value takes 20px (subtitle) and the incumbent 17px at weight 450 — the competitor column gets QUIETER, never louder, because emphasis is already spoken for by the white column.

label.purpose: Short all-caps machine strings: Archivo 600 11.5px at wdth 88, +0.09em. Replaces mono here — JetBrains Mono's fixed advance makes these ~1.8x wider and reads loose.

lead.purpose: Section decks: IBM Plex Sans 450 19px/1.5, max 56ch. Retires the old 17px !important patch that was compensating for a text face rendering small.

ledger-value.purpose: Spec-ledger stat values under the hero: Archivo 700 clamp(19px,1.7vw,24px) at wdth 92, tabular, over a 10.5px mono uppercase caption. text-transform:none is a required guard on the value — the li carries uppercase for the caption and it used to leak onto the value, stacking two all-caps registers.

extensions.roundedNote: pill (999px): scrollbar thumbs, status dots, home indicator only — controls squared at 6px. mark-compact (13px): XenAuth card mark at <=400px.

thirdPartyFidelity.rule: Inside the handset screen reproduce WhatsApp/iOS exactly; outside it use the XenTag system. Fidelity constants, not tokens — do not normalise.

chatFidelity.note: Handset shell and screen are concentric (38/30); composer pill 22; message bubble and quick-reply 10. Fidelity constants, not tokens.

dataBar.note: 2px on the 6px-tall paired-magnitude bars in the comparison ledger (and any future micro data furniture). A larger radius turns a 6px bar into a pill and changes its read; 2px keeps it a ruled mark.

iconography.stroke: 1.75px, one width per set, round caps + round joins
iconography.spacing: 2px minimum between sub-elements, <=3 elements at 16px render
iconography.color: monochrome currentColor; single accent token on the signal element only (ember/teal); never a second filled hue
iconography.productIdentity: products render as the object (label mock with real barcode/serial), drawn marks only for wayfinding chrome; integration logos are real brand glyphs, monochrome

tracking.rule: Optical tracking is a function of size, never a per-element nudge. Nine --ls-* steps crossing zero at ~17px.
tracking.onCharcoal: halve the positive branch — light-on-dark blooms optically

weightLadder.rule: Four text weights. 600 is emphasis and never appears inside a paragraph. 800 is Archivo-only and appears in exactly three places page-wide: hero h1, loss-register figures, footer wordmark.
weightLadder.fontSynthesis: none — Plex stops at 700 and Archivo at 900; without this a call past either end synthesizes a faux bold

rampExemptions: Object-printed type: text printed on a drawn physical object (the hero label render, dieline machine chips) scales with the object, not the reading ramp.
Third-party fidelity constants: the AskDemo WhatsApp thread, shipped as --wa-* custom properties.

emberPhrase.rule: Owner-directed, Aug 2026: reinstates a device from earlier versions of the site. Ember may colour the noun phrase that names what is being claimed — never the verb that makes the claim, and never more than a third of the heading's words.
emberPhrase.cap: Exactly three headings page-wide. A fourth turns a device into a tic.
emberPhrase.token: .h2-ember — Ember Dark #8E2D10 on bone, Ember Bright #F9762F on charcoal; the same hue does not hold contrast on both grounds.
theThree: #compare "Read it against what you run now"
#integrations "Works with the tools you already run"
stakes band "…a shipment you are insuring yourself"
emberPhrase.never: Never on the hero h1 — a two-tone extended-uppercase display line reads as gradient-adjacent, and the page's loudest voice stays one colour. Gradient text remains banned outright.

productMarks.rule: A product mark is a scale-reduced PORTRAIT OF THE OBJECT — the same label, the same tag — never a metaphor or a generic category glyph.
fiveRules: One envelope turned 90 degrees (both rx 2.5) — identical corner geometry does most of the family work
Two weights: contour 1.75 / detail 1.15, a 1.52:1 ratio
One accent, only on the signal element
One true quarter-arc centred on the mark own dot
Contact: XenTag dot sits ON the label edge and its arc leaves; XenAuth arc arrives from outside and stops ON the tag edge
productMarks.dark: strokes drop to 1.60/1.05 — a light-on-dark stroke reads ~1.25x heavier
productMarks.plate: 40px at radius 6px with a 26px glyph = 65% fill (the measured product-tile ratio). 55% is why the marks previously looked marooned. The plate stays NEUTRAL in both themes.
productMarks.floor: Compact variant below 24px; never render below 20px.

thirdPartyBrandMarks.rule: Vendor logos in the integrations hub are quoted artifacts, like the WhatsApp fidelity constants. Inside the plate, be the vendor; outside it, be XenTag.
thirdPartyBrandMarks.colourPolicy: Colour lives only inside a neutral bone plate, on the mark. ~0.23% of the hub surface.
thirdPartyBrandMarks.whyOnePlate: Raw brand colours on #151210 span 1.33:1 to 11.6:1 — an 8.7x luminance spread, which is what actually reads as a sticker sheet. One identical neutral plate collapses it to zero. Never tint a plate per vendor.

comparisonTable.sharedRefusals: Both refuse the same garnish: no zebra (anime.js compiled CSS has zero nth-child fills), no vertical rules, no per-row icons, no colour inside the grid, no row hover on reference text, and cells that never wrap.
comparisonTable.spec: Horizontal 1px --line hairlines only. No outer frame, no fill. One uniform 60px row. Cells 14px 20px; first column padding-left:0 so the table reads as ruled text flush with the prose margin. Headers demoted to machine metadata: 12px JetBrains Mono uppercase .08em Muted, never a fill bar. Footnote below the table.
comparisonTable.emphasis: One channel, and not text: a continuous Paper column behind the XenTag values. Ember stays out of the grid entirely, exactly as Watermelon keeps its brand green out of table cells.
comparisonTable.deleted: criterion glyphs, magnitude bars, win-dots, uppercase group bands, radio chips, the cloud well, disabled target pills — the fix was fewer elements, not smaller ones
comparisonTable.mobile: The never-wrap rule is deliberately traded away below 860px: a comparison only works if both values are visible, so the criterion wraps and all three columns stay on screen rather than scrolling sideways.

statRow.rule: Statistics never get a standalone surface. Neither Samsara nor Motive has a stats band anywhere; a stat row sits inside the claim section it supports, on the page ground, as bare type.
statRow.evidence: A full-page sweep of Motive's 10,339px homepage found zero elements matching a stat pattern at >=26px. Samsara runs three figures in a 128px row with no card, background, divider or footnote.
statRow.spec: Three figures at the top of #compare on bone. Each bounded by a 1px --line left rule with 16px padding (Motive cell anatomy). Figure clamp(34px,3.6vw,52px) condensed Archivo at weight 600 — dropped from 800 because at this size it reads as a poster rather than a measurement. 16px claim, 11px mono clickable source.

deAiRules: A decorative ring behind a diagram is ornament, not information.
Beams pulsing on a uniform stagger is the most recognisable generated-page tell. Structure stays; the metronome goes.
Three-line cards inside a connection diagram are copy nobody reads mid-diagram.

statusChips.rule: Status is a word, not a colour. Colour alone fails a colour-blind reader and fails in a screenshot, so every chip prints its state.
statusChips.spec: 10px JetBrains Mono 500, uppercase, .05em, 2px/7px padding, 4px radius (the chip step) on a 7-14% tint of its own hue.
statusChips.contrast: Measured at 10px against each tint: transit ember-dark 7.16:1, breach/geofence ember-dark 6.90:1, delivered signal-green-deep 5.60:1, stale muted 5.23:1. The raw palette values fail here (Signal Green 3.73:1, Ember Mid 3.20:1) — that is why the text uses darker derivations than the tint.

fleetMap.rule: The demo map is drawn, not photographed. It replaced a Web Mercator screenshot that could show coverage but not position.
fleetMap.projection: Equirectangular by construction: the viewBox IS degrees (0 0 360 180), so x = lng + 180 and y = 90 - lat, with no projection math anywhere.
fleetMap.link: One serial in three places — the pin takes a focus ring, the manifest row lights, a focus bar prints the live readings, and the phone header echoes the serial. All read the same projected state at answer time, so the panel and the thread can never disagree.

narrative.overview:
Operator-grade editorial: a $10 paper label sold like field equipment. The page reads as a broadsheet spec sheet — a bone-paper ground (#F5F2EA) whose every content section is framed by two vertical hairline rails, the way a broadsheet's column rules turn white space into a set measure. Live-platform moments (the walkthrough console, the integrations manifest, the CTA, the footer) sit on warm charcoal plates (#151210–#231D18) that carry no rails because they are their own plates. Cargo Ember (#BC3E10) is the only loud voice on the page: CTAs, live routes, active states, and exactly three underlined payoff words. Everything else argues with numbers, hairlines, and real footage.

The type does the selling. Archivo's variable width axis stretches the display voice wider as it gets bigger (h1 at 118% width, h2 at 110%, h3 at 106%), all at weight 800 — the extended-grotesque uppercase of freight stencils and equipment plates. Source Sans 3 carries every human-written sentence; JetBrains Mono is reserved for machine-sourced values (serials, temperatures, ETAs, API calls). Controls are squared and chunky at 6px radius — equipment buttons, not pills. Illustration is a single isometric hairline-dieline language: wireframe cartons, pallets, and radio arcs drawn in 1.1–1.6px strokes, never filled cartoons.

This world explicitly refuses the neon-dark AI-SaaS grammar: no two-tone gradient headlines, no glassmorphic decoration, no uppercase eyebrow label repeated over every section, no identical icon+heading+text card grids, no fabricated dashboards or reviews.
keyCharacteristics: Bone-paper broadsheet ground with per-section 1px vertical rails (hidden below 1080px)
Warm charcoal consoles for every live-platform moment; ember hairline seam across their top edge
Cargo Ember rationed to CTAs, live signals, and exactly three underlined payoff words
Archivo width-axis display (118%/110%/106%) at weight 800; mono strictly for machine values
Squared 6px controls with a 1px bottom ledge shadow and an arrow affordance
Hairline-first depth; deep soft ambient shadows only under whole consoles and physical objects
Isometric hairline dieline illustration system; real freight footage and label renders as imagery

rules.name: The Two Worlds Rule
rules.body: Every surface is either bone paper or warm charcoal console. No mid-gray third theme, no cool-toned dark, no section that can't say which world it belongs to.

rules.name: The Ember Budget Rule
rules.body: Cargo Ember is a signal, not a paint. On any daylight surface it appears only on CTAs, active states, live data, and payoff underlines — roughly ≤10% of the surface. If a section feels orange, it's over budget.

rules.name: The Teal Chip Rule
rules.body: Verified Teal exists only as small verified-state chips and the XenAuth mark's accent. It never grows into a section wash, a heading color, or a large surface.

rules.name: The Machine Voice Rule
rules.body: If a value comes from a device — a temperature, a battery percentage, a serial, an ETA, an event timestamp — set it in JetBrains Mono with tabular numerals. If a human wrote it, set it in Source Sans 3. Never mix within one string.

rules.name: The One Scale Rule
rules.body: Every section h2 on the page is the same voice: 800 / clamp(34px,4.4vw,56px) / 1.04 / -0.012em at 110% width. Sections differentiate by content and surface, never by inventing a new heading size.

rules.name: The Three Marks Rule
rules.body: The .h2-mark device — a thick ember underline (0.075em thickness, 0.16em offset, text-decoration-skip-ink: none) on inherited ink — appears exactly three times: the hero payoff ("can't afford to lose."), "close that gap.", and "One platform." A payoff word is never a second text color, and no new section may add a fourth mark without retiring one.

rules.name: The Hairline First Rule
rules.body: Reach for a 1px rule or a flat tonal step before any shadow or wash. A shadow is earned only by a whole console, a squared CTA's ledge, or a drawn physical object — never by a text block, list row, or inner tile.

dos: Do frame every bone-ground section with the .section-shell rails and keep dark bands rail-free — the contrast between measured paper and full-bleed plate is the layout's voice.
Do hold every section h2 to the One Scale (800 / clamp(34px,4.4vw,56px) / 1.04) and every machine value to JetBrains Mono tabular-nums.
Do keep controls squared at 6px with the 1px ledge shadow and an arrow affordance; panels normalize to 8px.
Do draw new illustrations in the isometric hairline-dieline language (1.1–1.6px wireframes, ember/teal only on the label and tap elements).

Do preserve the honest states: capture success only after a real 2xx, the failed state's mailto: fallback, prefers-reduced-motion kills (global animation kill, static gauge, unmasked scrollable marquee), and the marquee's hover/touch-hold pause.
Do signal "live" with green dots + glow and "route/active" with ember — and use warm charcoal (#151210 family) for any new dark surface, never cool gray.
donts: Don't add a fourth .h2-mark, a second text color inside a heading, or gradient text anywhere.
Don't exceed the Ember Budget — no ember section washes, tinted backgrounds beyond the ~0.07–0.12 active tints, or decorative orange.
Don't reintroduce generic-SaaS furniture: uppercase eyebrow labels over every section, identical icon+heading+text grids, glassmorphism beyond the nav's functional blur, emoji-as-icon.
Don't fabricate dashboards, reviews, or success UI — the platform section shows the production screenshot, captioned as such.
Don't put box-shadows on inner tiles, rows, or drawn objects (objects get drop-shadow filters), and don't glow anything that isn't a live signal.
Don't clip wide content silently — the comparison's right-edge fade is the pattern for horizontal overflow on narrow screens.
